To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the present study is the largest to date to evaluate associations of GWAS candidate SNPs with risk and size of uterine fibroids in a multi-ethnic population and that the study provides additional evidence for association of variants in the THSD7B and TNRC6B genes with uterine fibrosis.
we provide independent evidence that variants at the TNRC6B locus are associated with both risk and tumor size of UL.

the most significant association with risk in meta-analyses of GWAS and NIEHS-UFTS data was observed at TNRCB variants rs739181 and rs207285, and that THSD7B was associated with UL tumor size in pooled analyses.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of susceptibility genes for uterine fibroids, a common gynecologic condition with significant morbidity in women.
the evaluation of candidate susceptibility loci identified in two published GWAS in the NIEHS-Uterine Fibroid Study, a multiethnic study with a large sample size.
identification of novel genetic susceptibility loci for UL and provides further evidence of association of UL with TNRC6B and a novel association with THSD7B.

The main takeaway from our work is that
GWAS candidate susceptibility genes identified for UL in populations of European ancestry may be associated with UL risk and/or size in populations of African ancestry.
the association of TNRCB and THSD7B variants with UL is consistent in populations of African and European descent, but not in the Japanese.
genetic studies of UL are likely to yield more meaningful results when conducted in racially diverse populations.
